chapter_theme: A single short song at Thirumuruganpoondi (திருமுருகன்பூண்டி): a plea for the feet through ripened penance and prayer, with praise of Murugan as beyond the six faiths.

942.reading: The poet asks that, having pleaded many times for what is needful and come to know it, he ripen by touching penance and prayer and be granted Murugan's feet. The praise calls him hard for the six faiths to see, Siva's son, and the lord of Thirumuruganpoondi.
942.nuance: தவசெபமும் தீண்டிக் கனிவாகி: penance and japa are what ripen the soul for the feet. The line சவதமொடுந் தாண்டித் தக்ருர்வாய் is garbled and unread, and சிவகுமரன் பீண்டிற் பெயரானே may say that the town bears his name.

source_issues: Song 942: unflagged garble தக்ருர்வாய் (line 5); the ருர் sequence elsewhere in this run stands for ூர், so the word may be தக்கூர்வாய் or similar.
